chosen.premise: Galarian Articuno keeps the same 1.7-meter height but weighs 4.5 kilograms less and becomes Psychic/Flying.
chosen.hook: Articuno changes type and weight without changing height.
chosen.visualIdea: Split-screen Articuno forms: identical height markers, a 4.5-kilogram drop, and Ice replaced by Psychic.
chosen.note: The 1.7-meter height, 4.5-kilogram weight difference, and type swap are precise and fully supported, though regional-form comparisons can work for many Pokémon.

candidates.premise: Articuno is said to appear specifically to people who are doomed and lost in icy mountains.
candidates.hook: Seeing Articuno in the mountains may be a terrible sign.
candidates.visualIdea: A lost traveler follows footprints through a blizzard before Articuno appears above the ridge.
candidates.note: A sharply specific, unsettling rule found directly in Articuno’s Red entry: it appears to doomed people lost in icy mountains. The traveler-in-a-blizzard setup gives it strong narrative visuals.

candidates.premise: Articuno’s wing flaps chill the air so intensely that snow falls whenever it flies.
candidates.hook: For Articuno, flying is basically a weather event.
candidates.visualIdea: Articuno takes off; each wingbeat visibly drops the temperature and builds a snowfall trail behind it.
candidates.note: The Pokédex repeatedly supports the wingbeat-causes-snow mechanic, and it is highly visual, but weather creation is not uniquely Articuno’s concept.

candidates.premise: Articuno’s beautiful, seemingly translucent wings are said to be made of ice.
candidates.hook: Those wings may not be feathers at all—they may be ice.
candidates.visualIdea: Feather textures crystallize into translucent ice wings as Articuno spreads them in the sunlight.
candidates.note: The ice-wing claim is well supported, but saying the wings may not be feathers goes beyond the wording. The crystallization visual is excellent.

candidates.premise: Articuno turns airborne moisture into snow, and its strongest version of that process creates blizzards.
candidates.hook: Articuno doesn’t summon snow—it manufactures it from the air.
candidates.visualIdea: Floating moisture gathers around Articuno, freezes into flakes, then rapidly expands into a blizzard.
candidates.note: The air-to-snow mechanic is supported, but this substantially overlaps with flight-makes-snow. The claim that blizzards are the strongest version is an inference, not directly stated.

candidates.premise: Articuno stands alone as a legendary Pokémon with no evolution stage or transformation chain listed.
candidates.hook: Articuno arrives at its final form: there’s nowhere else to evolve.
candidates.visualIdea: An evolution chart builds with a single node—Articuno—while every possible next branch fades away.
candidates.note: The single-node evolution chain supports the presentation, but being unevolved is not a particularly surprising or distinctive fact for a legendary Pokémon, and the absence of evolution is inferred from the dataset. (Uniqueness capped at 2: its evidence is only fields every Pokémon has.)
